scope: Three purposively selected comparisons, one per subject pair; not an exhaustive search or a learned capability hierarchy.

records.title: Evidence supports an interpretation or an argument
records.proposal: The two expectations may share a narrow justification pattern: evidence is used to support an account or claim.
records.commonality: Both explicitly require evidence to do supporting work. This comparison is more specific than a shared occurrence of the word evidence, but it remains a builder interpretation of the two tasks.

axes.left: Cite textual evidence, analyze explicit/implicit meaning, and make logical inferences.
axes.right: Construct and present arguments using evidence.

axes.left: What a literary or informational text says.
axes.right: Attraction and dependence on masses and distance in gravitational interactions.
Evidence is required; simulation or digital-tool data and charts are examples, not mandatory formats.

axes.left: Supported textual analysis and logical inference; the standard does not prescribe one presentation format.
axes.right: A constructed and presented argument about the specified physical claim.

axes.left: Literary and informational scope (RI&RL) must be preserved.
axes.right: Assessment excludes Newton’s Law of Gravitation and Kepler’s Laws.

records.decision: Retain the narrow analogy for independent review. Do not merge the expectations or create a shared-skill, equivalence, prerequisite or transfer edge.
records.not_established: A common cognitive mechanism, transfer between subjects, equivalent assessments, or mastery of one through performance on the other.
records.next_evidence: Review the two source interpretations independently, then define a narrower relation and an explicit comparison rubric before proposing an ontology edge.
records.source_context: Science page 34 explicitly points MS-PS2-4 to 6-8.WHST.1, not to the modeled ELA 7R1. That source connection cannot be substituted for this candidate analogy.

evidence.source_locator: PDF/printed page 82; Grade 7 Reading, Key Ideas and Details; 7R1
evidence.quotation: Cite textual evidence to support an analysis of what the text says explicitly/implicitly and make logical inferences. (RI&RL)

evidence.source_locator: PDF/printed page 33; MS. Forces and Interactions; MS-PS2-4
evidence.quotation: Construct and present arguments using evidence to support the claim that gravitational interactions are attractive and depend on the masses of interacting objects and the distance between them.

records.title: A relationship between quantities is not automatically a proportional model
records.proposal: Treat representing a proportional relationship with an equation as equivalent to investigating forces, mass and motion.
records.commonality: Both concern relationships involving quantities. A mathematics application is conceivable, but the source tasks specify different performances.

axes.right: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence.
How changes in motion depend on the sum of forces and the object's mass.

axes.left: The wording does not require collecting experimental evidence.
axes.right: An investigation must provide evidence for the specified dependence.
An investigation and evidence; an equation is not required by this performance expectation.
Qualitative comparisons; assessment is one-dimensional, in an inertial frame, changing one variable at a time, without trigonometry.

records.decision: Reject the proposed equivalence because neither source task contains the other's required performance. This does not reject the possibility of using mathematics within a science investigation.
records.not_established: A proportional law from the word depends, a mandated equation, or a prerequisite relationship between these standards.
records.next_evidence: For a later application proposal, specify the variables, controlled conditions and mathematical relation, with source support. Review the page-34 math targets separately instead of substituting NY-7.RP.2c.
records.source_context: Science page 34 lists MP.2, NY-6.EE.2, NY-7.EE.3 and NY-7.EE.4 for MS-PS2-2. It does not list NY-7.RP.2c. Absence from this box is not proof that an application is impossible.

evidence.quotation: Represent a proportional relationship using an equation.

evidence.source_locator: PDF/printed page 33; MS. Forces and Interactions; MS-PS2-2
evidence.quotation: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object’s motion depends on the sum of the forces on the object and the mass of the object.

records.title: Explaining a graph point and interpreting a text remain distinct
records.proposal: Treat explaining the meaning of a proportional-graph point and analyzing a text as the same interchangeable expectation.
records.commonality: Both require giving an account of meaning in context. That broad resemblance does not erase the specified objects, evidence or constraints.

axes.left: Explain a graph point in terms of the situation.
axes.right: Cite textual evidence, analyze explicit/implicit meaning, and make logical inferences.

axes.left: A point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship.
axes.right: What a literary or informational text says.

axes.left: The task is grounded in a graph and its situation; it does not expressly require citing textual evidence.
axes.right: Textual evidence must support the analysis.

axes.left: An explanation of the point's contextual meaning, with specified special cases.
axes.right: Supported textual analysis and logical inference.
Grade 7; matching placement does not establish equivalence.

axes.left: Special attention to (0, 0) and (1, r), where r is the unit rate.
axes.right: Preserve both explicit/implicit analysis and literary/informational scope.

records.decision: Reject interchangeability. Keep the broader meaning-in-context resemblance as an observation in this record, not as an accepted shared capability.
records.not_established: That the standards assess the same skill, that one demonstrates the other, or that being in the same grade gives them a developmental dependency.
records.next_evidence: A future narrower analogy needs an operational definition and task-level evidence that preserves graph-specific and text-specific requirements.
records.source_context: This is a builder-selected comparison of the modeled math and ELA records, not a NYSED cross-reference between them.

evidence.quotation: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.
